chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated to us, from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: The stingy one is not the one who pays the obligatory alms-tax from his wealth and gives the final portion to his people. Rather, the truly stingy one is the one who withholds the obligatory alms-tax from his wealth and withholds the final portion from his people, and who is spendthrift in other than that.

key_terms.الْبَائِنَةَ: The final portion (often referring to a share given to kin or community)

ai.seo_question: What is the true definition of a stingy person in Shia hadith regarding zakat and family rights?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that true stinginess is defined by the neglect of obligatory dues (zakat) and the specific share of kin (al-baynah), distinguishing it from mere extravagance in other expenditures. This definition underscores the Shia emphasis on financial rights (huquq) as integral to faith, where withholding what is due to the community constitutes the core of avarice.

en.basel-kadem: 4.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ali Majilawayh, from his paternal uncle, Muhammed bin Abi’l-Qasem, from Muhammed bin Ali al-Kufi, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, that he said:

The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: The stingy is not the one who gives the obligatory alms tax from his property and grants the final to his people. Rather, the stingy, the truly stingy, is the one who prevents (the deduction of) the obligatory alms tax from his property, and who prevents (the giving of) the final to his people, and who spendthrifts in other than that.
